sources.entry: Goeland - Turns any RSS/Atom feed into a beautiful email digest. MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Goeland is a self-hosted tool that turns RSS, Atom, JSON, Imgur, and Miniflux sources into HTML email digests.
summary.what_it_does: Goeland fetches entries from configured sources (RSS/Atom/JSON feeds, Imgur tags, Miniflux instances, or merged sources) and runs them through a chain of composable filters. Filters include unseen (deduplication tracked in goeland.db), today, lasthours, retrieve (full-article fetch via CSS selector), language, reskip (regex title skip), limitwords, and digest/combine to bundle entries into one email. Pipes connect a source to a destination such as email, a terminal, or standalone HTML files. Emails use a responsive HTML template that can be customized. A built-in daemon mode runs each pipe on its own cron schedule, and the README also describes rate limiting, logging levels, and environment-variable configuration.
use_cases: Receive a daily or weekly email digest of RSS feeds
Email a summary of a subreddit or blog
Send unread Miniflux entries as an email digest
Merge several feeds on one topic into a single email
Write feed entries as standalone HTML files
Filter feed items by language, keyword, or age before sending
how_to_run: Download the latest binary from the release page and run: goeland run
Mount ./goeland.db:/data/goeland.db in Docker to persist unseen filter state
Edit config.toml to set the [email] SMTP details and define [sources] and [pipes]
Run goeland daemon to execute pipes on their cron schedules
notable: Composable, order-sensitive filter pipeline with over 20 filters
Built-in per-pipe cron scheduler, so no external cron is needed
Full-text retrieval of article content via CSS selectors
Can read unread or starred entries directly from a Miniflux instance
Pre-built binaries and Docker images for multiple platforms and architectures
caveats: Email delivery requires you to supply your own SMTP server credentials
Binary releases listed cover linux, darwin, and windows only, with no mobile or BSD builds
Miniflux sources only read entries by default, so the unseen filter or mark-as-read is needed to avoid repeats
Some features such as the image inliner and go-readability integration are listed only as roadmap items
